namespace: Canonical /api/v1 only; no parallel version API
wire_shape: Direct HTTP JSON. Adapt only through existing SDK transport response wrapper; no new backend envelope. UUIDs are strings; expires_at uses UTC Unix seconds. JSON snake_case is exact.
auth: Existing signed Manage session cookie required, then current Agentic-signed project-authority proof and identity revision. Inactive project/activation-only session fail closed before dispatch.

Agentic current project.settings.manage plus agents.run; require_thread_scope verifies current project_id/slug/Manage agent and thread owner. No new role, ACL, permission, membership or grant is introduced.
Service target stays in current signed-session enabled-service intersection and deployed project declaration; target service ACL remains as existing Manage proxy authority.
No browser actor/project/service trust or arbitrary target origin. Project and identity binding are server-resolved.

sse.rule: Persist validated action before emitting this reference. No executable body/arguments in this new event; old browser_action listeners cannot run it. Other browser tools retain browser_action. Load durable GET before showing a decision. Missing/failed capability never falls back to executeServiceAction plus completeAgentAction.

review_semantics: Read the action and capture version+payload_hash. Use a fresh operation UUID for every distinct edit/decision/execute; retries of the exact same operation must preserve its UUID and entire body.

Edit only body against the server-stored target and supported schema. Editing approved data returns to proposed, increments version and changes payload hash. Endpoint/schema catalog drift conflicts; it does not silently adopt a different schema.
Approve/reject requires a non-empty description and exact current version/hash. Rejection is terminal. Approval grants no permission and executes nothing.

Execute sends only operation_id, expected_version and payload_hash; any browser body/target/unknown field is rejected. Server claims approved action, persists dispatch intent, rechecks current authority and dispatches its saved payload.
Every transition uses one Mongo conditional replacement of state/version/hash and audit+response receipt. One claim/dispatch writer wins. Original terminal outcomes cannot be overwritten.

Exact completed operation replay returns its original response snapshot with replayed=true, after current scope checks. Different body reused with same action-local operation UUID conflicts. Execution replay resolves current durable receipt and never dispatches again.
A 409 requires a fresh GET. Do not silently retry with new version/hash or a new operation UUID. Editing/approval state can change across tabs.

Maximum reviewed input/payload is32KiB. Transition history is bounded (commands stop once it exceeds32 prior entries; automatic expiry is retained too); use explicit saves rather than per-keystroke writes. List returns newest50 summaries with no payload/history.
expiry_and_unknown: Review expires600 seconds from creation; expiry is server checked, independent of browser/SSE lifetime. Durable source key includes project/thread/user/run/tool identity. Missing durable project run refuses creation.
Claimed execution deadline60 seconds. Server target timeout20 seconds, no redirect following and no generic transport retry. Dispatch intent precedes the HTTP request.
Uncertain timeout/network/body-limit/non-2xx/202/207 returns outcome_unknown. A body-less2xx still has an authoritative HTTP status receipt, not independent database reconciliation.
After a lost/forged result reply, the client gets failure/unavailable and must query the durable action or retry the exact execute UUID. It must not submit the target again.

The current candidate does not auto-retry any target endpoint, including those that might support idempotency. Enabling retries later requires endpoint-specific evidence and a stable supported downstream key. No generic Idempotency-Key assertion is invented.
Unknown is terminal here; operator reconciliation is a separate future supported path, not a new generic retry control. Expired/unknown records and audit history are retained.

An HTTP cancellation or timeout does not cancel a claimed server action and is not proof of target failure. Reconcile by durable GET/identical execute operation; never create a new target request as a cancellation workaround.
schema_boundary: Uses the existing server ApiEndpoint catalog controlled by existing API_SERVICES_WRITE administration; selected endpoint method+service+canonical path and entire metadata hash are bound to the proposal. No model form, example payload or SDK string type is schema authority.

Only closed supported JSON-schema subset is accepted: type/properties/required/additionalProperties=false/items/enum/minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum with description/title. Nested optional schemas are checked too.

Refs, external schemas, arbitrary/open objects, schema examples/type-name placeholders and unsupported keywords explicitly make the operation unavailable. Existing catalogs predominantly containing examples will not become executable mutations.

Registered GET/DELETE with no body schema accepts only null body. Query keys must be registered, nonduplicate and have supported string/integer/number/boolean types; required query values are enforced.
Strict /api/v1 relative target, registered method/template match, no path percent-encoding/traversal/backslash/fragment/external origin. Body edit cannot alter service/method/path.
Catalog rollout/import of authoritative structured schemas is not performed or implicitly authorized by this candidate. No claim that every deployed operation is currently available.

internal.commands: edit|approve|reject from public review bridge; claim|dispatch|finish only inside Manage execution. Internal command also carries result and execution_id, never accepted from public review. Legacy browser/actions/{id}/complete rejects durable manage_sdk and has no fallback.

fields: fresh nonce UUID for each bridge call
request_proof.lifetime: Manage mints15 seconds; Agentic requires nonnil nonce/op, at most30 second lifetime, <=2 second future skew and nonexpired exact scope/body. Commands cross-check version/hash/op against signed body.

fields: hash of the entire exact request proof including fresh nonce
hash of the returned canonical JSON
response_proof.lifetime: 15 seconds; Manage checks purpose, exact request hash, body hash, <=2 second future skew, max15 second age/lifetime, and no response before request. Missing/malformed/tampered/wrong-request/old replay is unavailable, never authority. All successful read/list/command receipts are signed. Error responses can only deny; they never authorize target execution.
response_proof.exposure: Internal headers/proofs are consumed by Manage and not forwarded to the browser.

internal.canonicalization: SHA256 over recursive sorted JSON object keys; array order and exact string/query content preserved. This is a semantic source/payload hash, not a Git commit hash.

precise_runtime_delta: No new key/env is provisioned. Reuses existing per-project signing derivation exactly: SHA256 of <first nonblank WORKER_SHARED_SECRET else CLOUD_WORKER_SECRET>:<project>:manage, preserving configured seed bytes; HMAC-SHA256 over existing token format. Both backends must resolve the same configured seed; missing/incompatible keys fail closed. Synthetic local fixture seeds only in tests.

Trust expansion is explicit: the already trusted per-project Manage server signing identity can now request payload-bound action decisions/claims/results; purpose-separated request and response verification additionally binds every operation. No platform user/session or actor-label flag alone grants this.

AGENTIC_INTERNAL_URL remains the existing approved private Agentic origin. Keep existing service ingress trust isolation and current project-authority signing configuration. No live networking/CORS/security configuration changed.

New Mongo collection manage_agent_actions, unique default _id, plus manage_actions_scope compound index. Creation validates/persists before SSE. Existing Mongo account needs its established collection/index privileges. No SQL migration, preset, role seed or destructive rollback.

Rollback requires disabling durable UI/actions without fallback; retain action/audit records and matching server versions. Do not roll back one side into accepting unsigned replies or legacy completion.
Two backend candidates and actual sole-owner SDK/UI integration must be deployed together under controller approval; no SDK pack or shared panel/Docker/package/lock source changed here.
